description: Karnataka has cleared the launch of a new artificial intelligence centre in Bengaluru to boost AI use and deeptech innovation. The facility, set up with NASSCOM, will support startups, MSMEs and research institutions across key technology areas. The Rs 20-crore project aims to strengthen the state’s position as a hub for applied AI.
body_lead: Karnataka approved the establishment of an artificial intelligence centre of excellence (AI-CoE) on Thursday to accelerate AI adoption, deeptech innovation, and digital transformation across sectors. The state plans to establish the facility, named the Centre for Applied AI for Tech Solutions (CATS), in Bengaluru in partnership with NASSCOM. The project requires an outlay of Rs 20 crore over four years.
